FILER'S CORRECTION — read this BEFORE designing the fix. It demotes the framing in the task body.

I filed this task's body before enumerating the dispatch window on #2054. That
enumeration changes the diagnosis materially.

WHAT THE BODY SAYS: the owner-blind terminate guard is the primary gap — a
non-owner can self-post the upload-verification PASS and destroy a live owner's
pod, and nothing in the surface catches it.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY TRUE: the surface DID carry the catch, and it was skipped.
`spec-ladder-2054` posted a `[long-phase-heartbeat]` on #2054 at 19:27:39Z
reading, verbatim: "pod=pod-2054-tiers pilot PASS ... Production launched
19:26Z ... fence re-sized to 2x = 4 h (alarm ~23:30Z) ... launcher pid 1763."
That is an explicit live-owner declaration with an unexpired fence, sitting in
the durable record two hours before the 21:32:37Z teardown. The pre-dispatch
external-marker triage duty (SKILL.md Step 9 entry guard) is exactly the
mechanism that surfaces such a marker, and the orchestrator skipped it — the
watcher's triage-observer had already flagged the same omission twice earlier
the same day (17:33:03Z, 19:53:02Z) before flagging the 22:11:10Z dispatch.

REVISED SCOPE — do NOT over-build:
  - PRIMARY failure was execution discipline against an EXISTING duty. No new
    detection mechanism is required to have prevented this incident. Resist
    designing one.
  - The owner-blind guard is a REAL but SECONDARY defense-in-depth gap: a
    correctly-triaged non-owner could still terminate, because
    `_guard_upload_verification_before_terminate` asks only whether some PASS
    marker with an `outroot=` token exists, never who owns the pod, while
    CLAUDE.md scopes the grant to "the agent actively driving a job on a pod it
    provisioned" in prose no code reads.
  - Therefore prefer the SMALLEST change that closes the secondary gap. The
    highest-value single check is fence-awareness: refuse (or require an
    explicit override) when the task carries an owner heartbeat/fence whose
    deadline is in the FUTURE. Note the shape carefully — a fence is OLD by
    construction and still binding, so the #2111 pre-stop probe's
    "breadcrumb younger than ~10 min" recency test structurally cannot detect
    it. Recency is the wrong predicate here; deadline-in-future is the right one.
  - Body items 2 (owner attribution on the PASS) and 3 (non-owner surface-for-
    approval path) remain reasonable but are lower priority than item 1, and
    should not grow into a general ownership-tracking subsystem.
  - Body item 4 stands unchanged: add conditions, never remove the existing
    upload-verification or `outroot=` (#2187) checks.

A cheap, high-value companion worth considering in the same round: make the
triage-observer's finding HARDER TO IGNORE for repeat offences on the same task
within a session — three identical flags in one day on #2054 produced no
behaviour change. That is a surfacing-strength question, not a new detector.

NO DATA WAS LOST in the incident: uploads were complete (113/113 verified
independently), teardown went through the gated path with `outroot=swept-clean`,
and the owner's own re-merge confirmed byte-equality with the harvested commit.
The benign outcome owed to clean uploads, not to the mechanism.

The task body is a spec (four numbered fix constraints + a `## Constraints`
block), and every gap I could have asked about is answered by the code or by

inherit the same reading rather than re-deriving it.

## Context resolved from project knowledge

**1. The guard and the grant it opens (the exact fix surface).**
- `scripts/pod_lifecycle.py:3472` `_guard_upload_verification_before_terminate(issue, *, skip_flag, dry_run)` — returns early on `dry_run`; returns on any unresolvable task (`FileNotFoundError` / `RuntimeError` / `ValueError`, warn-and-proceed); returns on `kind != "experiment"` (kind defaults to `"experiment"` when absent, fail-safe); then reads the LATEST `epm:upload-verification` note and returns iff it records PASS **and** carries the `outroot=` token (#2187). Two `SystemExit` refusals: PASS-without-token (3563) and no-PASS-at-all (3596).
- Call site `scripts/pod_lifecycle.py:3817` in `cmd_terminate`, ordered AFTER `_guard_keep_running_before_terminate` (3803, #1485) and BEFORE any live-API mutation.
- Passing the guard is what opens the grant: `_verified_teardown_grant(...)` (3750) wraps the `terminate_pod` loop at 3853, and `backends/kill_approval.py` `verified_teardown` (L58) / `verified_teardown_active` (L86) make `compute_kill_approved()` (L103) return True inside it (L117). So the guard's boolean IS the authorization — nothing downstream re-checks ownership. That is precisely the owner-blindness the task reports.

**2. Owner attribution has NO existing channel to read — the fix must create one.** `events.jsonl` rows carry exactly `ts, kind, version, by, note` (`task_workflow.post_event`, L5264-5310), and `by` **defaults to the literal `"unknown"`** (L5269; `scripts/task.py:1684` `p.add_argument("--by", default="unknown")`). Confirmed on the incident itself: the owner's fence heartbeat and the harvester's PASS are BOTH `by=unknown`. Only machine posters self-identify (`task.py`, `task_state shim`, `autonomous_session_watch`, `spawn_session-stop`). No session-identity env var is exported either (this session has `EPM_AUTONOMOUS_SESSION` / `HAPPY_AUTOMATED_SESSION` but no session id); `~/.eps-autonomous/issue-<N>.json` carries `happy_session_id` but is per-ISSUE, not per-round, and a parked-task inline round need not be registered. Consequence for the plan: constraint 2 is not "read the existing attribution field" — it is "establish an attribution token on the launch side and require the PASS to match it".

**3. Fences are likewise PROSE today, and `fence=` is already TAKEN with a different meaning.** The incident's fence lived inside an `epm:progress` note as free text (`[long-phase-heartbeat] ... alarm 23:30Z`, #2054 v306 at 19:27:39Z). Repo-wide grep finds no `fence_until=` / `deadline=` / owner-fence token convention. `fence=` DOES exist in `epm:run-launched` (`.claude/agents/experimenter.md:892-954`) but means the SERVER-side max-run-duration kill (`<hours>h` on GCP, `none` on RunPod) — a new owner-fence token must not collide with it. `[long-phase-heartbeat]` is a real machine-read token (`autonomous_session_watch.py:2262`) but it is read for RECENCY (`LONG_PHASE_HEARTBEAT_FRESH_S`, 90 min default, L2781), which the task body explicitly rules out as the test.

**4. Incident timeline, from #2054's own events (constraint 1's evidence).** 19:20:43Z `epm:run-launched v39` (`pod=pod-2054-tiers`, cpu-bigmem) → 19:27:39Z owner heartbeat + fence to 23:30Z → **21:32:37Z `epm:upload-verification v38` `by=unknown`, `Verdict: PASS ... outroot`-bearing, posted by the non-owner** → terminate passed the guard → 22:45:06Z `epm:progress v314` records the correction: *"Owner agent ALIVE — the af64a3c4af commit message's 'owner-agent death' premise was wrong: this session was inside its own posted fence (19:27Z heartbeat, alarm 23:30Z)."* Marker recency could not have caught it: the fence was ~2 h old by construction and still binding.

**5. Adjacent guards that do NOT cover this, so the fix is additive rather than a re-tune.** The `keep-running` shield (#1485) is set/unset by the owner and was SET here — the watcher logged three `pod-keep-running-skip` exemptions on 08-13 — yet it does not gate the surgical `--name-suffix` path (`_guard_keep_running_before_terminate` returns immediately at 3627 when `name_suffix is not None`), which is the path a suffixed follow-up pod is torn down by. The #2111 pre-stop probe keys on a ~10-min breadcrumb and structurally cannot see a 2 h fence.

**6. Established precedents the plan should reuse rather than invent.** For the "explicit override" in constraint 1: `--force-keep-running` (`getattr(args, "force_keep_running", False)`, threaded at 3806) is the in-file precedent for an operator override on a terminate guard — and it is NOT one of the user-only approval channels, so it stays inside the standing prohibition on `--approve` / `EPS_ALLOW_COMPUTE_KILL=1` / `EPS_ALLOW_POD_TERMINATE=1`. For constraint 3's non-owner route: the surface-for-approval shape already specified in `.claude/rules/pods.md` (marker + push naming the pod and its hourly burn, pod left alive). For the pod-name key: `epm:run-launched` notes already LEAD with `pod=<name>` in structured position (#1961), and `cmd_terminate` already resolves `--name-suffix` to the canonical name at 3821 — so a per-pod owner/fence lookup has a key available without a schema change.

## Readings I am fixing now (stated, not asked — autonomous session)

Both follow forcibly from `## Constraints` ("must not block the legitimate ask-free case"; "must not introduce a path that terminates pods MORE readily"), so they are auto-continuation assumptions, not user questions:

- **Assumption:** the new conditions bind only when their evidence EXISTS. No pod carries an owner token or a structured fence today, so absent/unparseable evidence ⇒ proceed exactly as today (never a new refusal); PRESENT + unexpired fence, or PRESENT owner token that the PASS fails to match ⇒ refuse (or require the explicit override). Fail-CLOSED on absent evidence would block every legitimate Step-8 teardown on the fleet.
- **Assumption:** the existing PASS + `outroot=` checks and both `SystemExit` refusal messages are preserved byte-for-behavior; the fix adds a condition ahead of the grant, and `--skip-upload-verify` keeps its documented never-ran-pod semantics.

## Non-blocking, carried into the plan as scope questions

- Whether the fence/owner token is a NEW `epm:` marker kind or a note token on the existing `epm:run-launched` / `epm:progress` surface (both satisfy the spec; the token surface is a plan §-scope call for the critic ensemble, and `workflow.yaml § markers` changes are a public-contract surface worth naming explicitly).
- Emitter-side adoption: a guard that reads a token nothing emits is inert, so the plan must name which surfaces start emitting it (`.claude/rules/pods.md` completion-side teardown recipe, the `/issue` Step 8 path, the CLAUDE.md inline-round pre-launch signals) — the built-but-stranded-fix failure mode from `.claude/rules/workflow-fix-on-bug.md`.
